newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cesp sees dollar bond by March.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cesp sees dollar bond by March.

text.p: Sao Paulo state power company Cesp hopes in March to launch a $200 million Eurobond, the first tranche of a $500 million debt program it plans this year, Cesp international affairs chief Octavio de Barros said.
"Our intention is to go to the market in March with a $200 million Eurobond," Barros told Reuters.
He said Cesp would probably launch a second bond by the end of the first semester.
"But we don't know the size of the second issue or whether it will be in dollars. There are interesting possibilities in Deutsche mark, Italian lire and yen," he said.
Cesp might issue a third bond in by September, but Barros said it was too early to tell.
He refused to say what the maturity would be on the $200 million bond, adding that information and the lead manager for the deal could be announced on Friday.
In addition to the $500 million Eurobond issue planned for 1997, Cesp also intends to draw on $50 million from a $255 million outstanding Euro commercial paper program, Barros said.
Cesp is tapping international capital markets to reduce its expensive short-term domestic debt, which now makes up 48 percent of the power firm's 11 billion reais ($10.5 billion) debt.

"This is the single most important thing we have to do to get our finances in order," Barros said. He noted that since 1995 the company has managed to cut the portion of its domestic debt to 48 percent from 60 percent of total obligations.
